input.candidate_text:
Let \(G\) and \(H\) be nonabelian groups of order \(21\). By Sylow’s theorems, the number of Sylow \(7\)-subgroups divides \(3\) and is congruent to \(1\pmod 7\), so each group has a unique, hence normal, Sylow \(7\)-subgroup.

For \(G\), choose generators \(b\) of a Sylow \(7\)-subgroup and \(a\) of a Sylow \(3\)-subgroup. Their intersection is trivial, so \(G=\langle b\rangle\langle a\rangle\), and every element has a unique expression \(b^s a^r\), where \(0\le s<7\) and \(0\le r<3\).

Since \(\langle b\rangle\) is normal, conjugation by \(a\) gives
\[
aba^{-1}=b^i
\]
for some \(i\in\{1,\dots,6\}\). Because \(a^3=e\), conjugating three times gives \(b=b^{i^3}\), hence \(i^3\equiv1\pmod 7\). The solutions are \(i=1,2,4\). If \(i=1\), then \(a\) and \(b\) commute and generate \(G\), making \(G\) abelian, a contradiction. Thus \(i=2\) or \(4\). In the latter case, replacing \(a\) by \(a^{-1}\) changes the exponent to \(4^{-1}\equiv2\pmod 7\). Therefore we may choose \(a,b\) so that
\[
a^3=b^7=e,\qquad aba^{-1}=b^2.
\]

Applying the same argument to \(H\), choose generators \(c,d\) such that
\[
c^3=d^7=e,\qquad cdc^{-1}=d^2,
\]
and every element of \(H\) has a unique expression \(d^s c^r\).

Define
\[
\phi:G\to H,\qquad \phi(b^s a^r)=d^s c^r.
\]
This is well-defined by uniqueness of the normal forms. Since
\[
a^r b^t a^{-r}=b^{2^r t},
\]
we have
\[
(b^s a^r)(b^t a^u)=b^{s+2^r t}a^{r+u}.
\]
The identical formula holds in \(H\), so \(\phi(xy)=\phi(x)\phi(y)\). Hence \(\phi\) is a homomorphism. It is bijective because it maps the unique \(21\) normal forms \(b^s a^r\) to the unique \(21\) normal forms \(d^s c^r\). Therefore \(G\cong H\). Thus any two nonabelian groups of order \(21\) are isomorphic.
input.theorem: Prove that any two nonabelian groups of order 21 are isomorphic.
